clue.text: Unkempt, quiet kind of cat, with little time left

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: with the time abbreviation left out, it is removed from the cat's name

parts.note: a tabby is a striped cat
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A scruffy, quiet sort of cat with little time remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as remaining, but here it means taken away: the time abbreviation is dropped from the striped cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unkempt looks shabby, worn and untidy.

clue.text: Trains some sea creatures altogether

definitions.meaning: to train or educate someone, as a verb
fish swimming together form groups with this collective name

explanation.surface: Trains and some sea creatures, all together.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train; a school is also a group of fish swimming together.

clue.text: It's said ironically to give precedence

definitions.text: It's said ironically to give precedence

parts.words: It's said ironically to give precedence
parts.note: a mock-courteous phrase used when letting an older person go through a door first

explanation.surface: A remark someone makes ironically while waving another person ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the old jibe lets an elder go first, implying the speaker is the better looking.

clue.text: See 2
A dry beer drunk with pumpernickel

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dry beer downed alongside some dark German bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals an anagram of A DRY BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: pumpernickel is a dense dark bread made from rye flour.

clue.text: The yellow tie mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for tie is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a yoke is a bond or tie joining two things

explanation.surface: A yellow necktie being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' says YOKE is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow of an egg is its central part, as opposed to the white.

clue.text: Inspired article welcomed by staff of Life

indicators.note: being welcomed by means being taken inside, so the article goes within the staple food

parts.note: bread is proverbially the staff of life
the definite article

explanation.surface: An inspired piece of writing taken on by the staff of Life magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff of Life' looks like a magazine's employees but is the proverbial name for bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is literally to draw in air, so inspired means breathed in.

clue.text: She's not completely above the law

indicators.note: only part of these words is taken, so the name sits inside them

explanation.surface: A woman who is not entirely above the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' marks the name hidden in abovE THE Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's name stands for a female person, a she.

clue.text: Shows what Roman policy does in Scotland?

definitions.meaning: portrays or represents, as a verb

definitions.text: what Roman policy does in Scotland?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., getting rid of the Picts, the people Rome fought in Scotland

explanation.surface: Shows what Roman strategy did north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something in a picture is to portray or represent it.

clue.text: Spotted carnivores with a sense of humour?

definitions.meaning: African scavenging predators with dappled coats
these animals are famous for their laughing cry

explanation.surface: Spotted meat-eaters that seem to enjoy a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted species of these predators is known as the laughing kind for its giggling call.

clue.text: Risqué golf shot that usually pays off

parts.note: blue jokes are risqué or smutty
a chip is a short lofted golf shot onto the green

explanation.surface: A cheeky golf shot that usually comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are reliable investments from sound companies, usually yielding a return.

clue.text: Accurate summary given poor grade

parts.note: a précis is a short summary of a text
E is a low exam grade

explanation.surface: An accurate summary that still earns a bad mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: accurate and exact both mean correct in every detail.

clue.text: Upset by obvious run-out

parts.note: overt means open and obvious

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of run are rearranged

explanation.surface: Upset by an obvious run-out at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-out' looks like a cricket dismissal; 'out' is the anagram signal on RUN, making URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something, such as a boat or a verdict, is to overturn it.

clue.text: One's inclined to be emphatic

parts.note: a sloping typeface used for emphasis in print

explanation.surface: Someone tends to be forceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined' reads as tending, but it means literally sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: this sloping style of type is used to stress words.

clue.text: Shooting in Dynasty following endless row

indicators.note: following puts the dynasty after the shortened row
endless means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a file is a line or row, as in single file
the Ming dynasty ruled China

explanation.surface: Shooting scenes for the TV soap Dynasty after an endless argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line, FILE, which loses its end to give FIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting a scene is recording it on camera, the work of a film crew.

clue.text: Talking posh may also be frowned upon

definitions.text: Talking posh may also be frowned upon

parts.words: Talking posh may also be frowned upon
parts.note: put the answer after the first word and you get a social sin like speaking affectedly; posh is also its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Speaking in a plummy accent can also attract disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: Talking about work at a party is frowned upon, just like talking posh, whose letters it rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: talking about work in company is a familiar social faux pas.

clue.text: Old copyists representing mostly river scenes

indicators.note: representing suggests the letters being shown in a new form
mostly means not quite all the letters are used, one being dropped

explanation.surface: Old copyists painting what are mostly riverside scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops one E from RIVER SCENES; 'representing' signals an anagram of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Scriveners were clerks who copied documents by hand before printing.

clue.text: Strange tail-less male with needle-like teeth?

indicators.note: strange signals the letters forming an odd new arrangement
tail-less means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd male creature with sharp, needle-pointed teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' signals an anagram of MAL (male without its tail) plus NEEDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are coated with a hard glossy layer of the substance named, so they are coated that way.

clue.text: Stupid pair join in naming the killer

indicators.note: join adds the following word on to the end
a pair means two of the same word

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A dim-witted couple help identify the murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an assassin is a killer, usually of a public figure.

clue.text: Frank's English likewise said to gain entrance

parts.note: frank means open, and with 's it becomes the word plus S
the same means likewise

explanation.surface: Frank's English is said to do just as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba's magic password opened the robbers' cave, so it is said to get in.

clue.text: See 20
You need to soak Goldsmith's biscuits

parts.note: a bath is something you take for a soak
Oliver Goldsmith was the Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield, so his first name plus the 's

explanation.surface: These biscuits need dunking, according to a goldsmith.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath Olivers are plain English dry biscuits, often eaten with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are a traditional plain biscuit created by a Bath physician.

clue.text: The pale sort of liquor seen at bottom of glass

definitions.text: liquor seen at bottom of glass

indicators.note: sort here suggests sorting the letters into another order

explanation.surface: Pale ale left at the bottom of the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' signals an anagram of THE PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the dregs of drink left in the bottom of a glass.

clue.text: Dad's in pain, pehaps being brave

indicators.note: in puts the father inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is a word for dad, and 's means is

explanation.surface: Dad is in pain, perhaps being stoic about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' seems an adjective, but is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a warrior of this Native American people is called a brave.

clue.text: Stirring finale recalling 24 eg at springtime

indicators.note: stirring means mixing the letters up

explanation.surface: A stirring finale to a piece recalling a spring flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' looks like an adjective praising the finale but is the anagram signal. 24 is LILAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub such as lilac puts out fresh foliage in spring.

clue.text: For Olive's relation ring up about one

indicators.note: about means going around the numeral
up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Phoning a relation of Olive's about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a woman, but is the tree; LLAC goes about I.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive and this flowering shrub belong to the same plant family.

clue.text: Slimmer's chocolate ration, perhaps, if she's to look good in it!

definitions.text: Slimmer's chocolate ration, perhaps, if she's to look good in it!

parts.words: Slimmer's chocolate ration, perhaps, if she's to look good in it!
parts.note: a dieter allows herself a single square of chocolate to fit a swimming costume

explanation.surface: A dieter's single square of chocolate, needed to look good on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a swimsuit in a single garment, and the dieter's lone bit of chocolate.

clue.text: Starts to drive everywhere by taxi? You'll soon get into it!

indicators.note: the starts of these words, each giving its opening letter

explanation.surface: Taking taxis everywhere will soon land you in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending freely on cabs lands you owing money, in the red.

clue.text: Wiggly lines young Edward joined up

indicators.note: wiggly suggests a twisting, rearranged line of letters

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Little Edward joining up wiggly lines, as in a dot-to-dot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enlist is to join up, especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: A month without Leo playing the cat

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the month wraps round

parts.note: Oct is short for October

indicators.note: playing suggests the name being toyed with, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A month without Leo the lion playing the part of a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but its old sense is outside: the month wraps round the shuffled star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: It can explain to teacher why you don't appear to be educated

definitions.text: It can explain to teacher why you don't appear to be educated

parts.words: It can explain to teacher why you don't appear to be educated
parts.note: a parent's letter excusing a pupil's absence from school through illness

explanation.surface: Something that tells a teacher why you seem so ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't appear to be educated' seems to mean look ignorant but means fail to turn up for lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a doctor's or parent's letter justifying absence through illness.

clue.text: Take the mickey when seconds finally arrive

parts.note: to end up is to arrive in the end

explanation.surface: Mock someone when the second helpings finally turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the mickey' is British slang for mock or tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to parody or ridicule someone is to mock them.
